model: segmentation-models-pytorch Unet with EfficientNet-B4 encoder (ImageNet, smp-hub), full-res decoder, 1-ch input, pointwise log norm, focal x10 + dice; best val checkpoint (step 10000) of h1 run smp_effb4; 4-flip TTA; threshold 0.9995 picked on 300 val images
based_on: smp_unet efficientnet-b4 (h1 run smp_effb4, best.pt step 10000; recipe of h7 smp_r34_a)

eval.eval_cmd: python -m seg.evaluate --model smp_unet --config configs/smp_effb4.yaml --ckpt /sdf/data/lcls/ds/prj/prjcwang31/results/peaknet-seg-sprint/checkpoints/h1/smp_effb4/best.pt --split test --split-json results/split/result.json --peak-label 1 --workers 8 --thr 0.9995 --tta --out test_metrics.json --save-overlays overlays --n-overlays 4   (threshold+TTA chosen on val by: python scripts/val_grid.py --member smp_unet:<best.pt> --n 300 -> /sdf/data/lcls/ds/prj/prjcwang31/results/peaknet-seg-sprint/evals/h1/smp_effb4/grid_best.json)

notes: Final best_model (04:35). Chosen by VAL: h1's smp Unet-effb4 with flip TTA at thr 0.9995 scores val peak F1 0.9272 on 300 evenly spaced val images (scripts/val_grid.py, grid_best.json; last.pt only 0.899), above h7's final1 ensemble (Unet-r34 last + UNet++-r34 best, TTA, thr .70) at 0.9251 on 300 val images; on the whole test split (1529 images) it scores peak F1 0.9217 (P .896, R .949) vs final1 0.9182. Trained by h1 with h7's seg.train recipe (focal x10 + dice, crop 512, 16 crops/step, pos_frac .8, lr 5e-4, norm_log). A 4-member ensemble incl. effb4 (final2) was cancelled before its test pass: its val selection (sweep capped at .99, which under-rates the very confident effb4) gave 0.9220 < these. History of best_model: 0.9061 (r34 snapshot) -> 0.9141 (UNet++) -> 0.9182 (final1 ensemble) -> 0.9217 (this). Findings: full-res decoders matter for 1-2 px peaks; FPs are confident spots that look like real unlabeled peaks (precision cap ~0.9 from labels); post-processing did not help; flip TTA +0.002-0.004; focal x10 models are very confident, so sweep thresholds to 0.9999.
